datasets.title: Damage assessment along the Debed river in Tumanian Municipality, Lori Province, Armenia as of 29 May 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240528ARM, GDACS ID: 1102647 This map illustrates satellite based structure damage assessment along the Debed river in Tumanian Municipality, Lori Province as observed from a Pléiades imagery acquired on the 29 May 2024 at 11:39 local time. UNOSAT observed 113 potentially affected buildings, 12 potentially affected bridges, 16 potentially affected road segments and 5 potentially affected railway segments. Based on Worldpop population data, about 3,000 people live within 200m from the Debed river. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/damage-assessment-along-the-debed-river-in-tumanian-municipality-lori-province-armenia-as-]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts conducted post-event damage assessment by comparing Pléiades satellite imagery acquired on 29 May 2024 with reference imagery to identify structural damage along the Debed river. Building and infrastructure damage counts were extracted through visual interpretation, and population exposure was estimated by intersecting Worldpop gridded population data with a 200m buffer around the river. This preliminary satellite-based assessment provides rapid damage estimates for humanitarian response.
